name: AureliusPromptus
oneLiner: Multi-tenant SaaS for managing LLM prompts: five deployed .NET 9 services, four Next.js front ends, ten Fly.io apps.
summary: Storing, versioning, reviewing and publishing LLM prompts, plus an agent layer that extracts a master prompt from a saved conversation. The backend is five ASP.NET Core services on `net9.0`, which `AppHost.cs` registers with .NET Aspire and which `flyio.yml` actually deploys (authservice, prompttemplatesservice, agenticservice, marketplaceservice, extensionservice); four of them have their own database (`authdb`, `prompttemplatesdb`, `agenticdb`, `marketplacedb`), ExtensionService has none; the front end is four Next.js 14 applications and a hand-written Manifest V3 extension that injects prompts on eight AI chat hosts. The AI layer is thinner than the name suggests: `FlowEngine.cs` is 229 lines of a JSON step interpreter, and the repository's own assessment from August 2026 states outright that 'agent' here means a system prompt plus a model deployment. The most interesting engineering decision sits in `DatabaseProviderExtensions.cs`: 188 lines that switch between SQL Server, PostgreSQL and InMemory with a single switch and translate a `.flycast` host to `.internal`. Thanks to them the migration from Azure Container Apps to Fly.io happened without forking a single service. The real asset of this repository is therefore the deployment, not the AI.
license: No LICENSE file at the root; MIT sits only in `AureliusPromptus.Web.Portal/LICENSE` (Copyright (c) 2024 Konrad Cinkusz), and the README's licence section is a placeholder.
tests: 204 `[Fact]`/`[Theory]` attributes across five xUnit projects (AgenticService 69, AuthService 48, PromptTemplatesService 36, MarketplaceService 31, AgentTemplatesService 20); `[Theory]` produces more cases than attributes, so the actual count is higher and has not been verified. The front end has three Jest test files in the Portal, and the whole E2E layer was handed over to a separate repository and does not run here in anything.
ci: Nine workflows, 3,709 lines of YAML: `pr-validation.yml` builds conditionally according to the changes it detects (lint + Jest + build for the Portal, lint + build only for the three other front ends, restore + build + test for the five .NET services). `flyio.yml` is 86 KB, provisions Azure through Bicep, builds only the changed services, pushes images to `registry.fly.io` and deploys them in an explicitly fixed dependency order; the E2E tests are not wired into any workflow.

The real state of test automation

components.name: Infrastruktura Bicep i skrypty Fly.io
components.description: 24 Bicep modules, in which every service gets its own managed identity and its own role assignments to SQL, rather than one shared account. Next to it a `flyio/` directory with PowerShell scripts for setup, scaling, DNS and destroying environments.

components.name: The deployment pipeline
components.description: `flyio.yml` detects changed services, builds only those and deploys them in an explicit dependency order, starting an ephemeral machine to provision agents as a versioned deployment artefact. `private-cloud-push.yml` deliberately stops at pushing images to the client's ACR and leaves the deployment to their team.

components.name: AureliusPromptus.ServiceDefaults
components.description: 1,365 lines of extensions over `IHostApplicationBuilder`. Beyond the {{term:servicedefaults}} template ({{term:otel}}, health, discovery, resilience) it adds JWT authentication, a CORS policy, Swagger with JWT, a validation filter and `DatabaseProviderExtensions`, which picks SQL Server, PostgreSQL or InMemory from a single switch. The extension signatures themselves are purely infrastructural, but the library's public surface carries a domain type: `public sealed record KonradPromptSeed(string Name, string Icon, string Content, string Tags)` and `public static class KonradPromptSeeds` with `public static readonly IReadOnlyList<KonradPromptSeed> Published` and `Internal` (607 lines of one author's prompt content). On top of that `Services/QuotaConsumptionService.cs` sits in the `PromptTemplatesService.Services` namespace and exposes `Task<bool> CheckAndConsumeAsync(string? authorizationHeader, string quotaType)`, which calls `POST /api/auth/quota/consume` in AuthService. Moving this to another product therefore requires cutting the domain out first, not merely adding a reference — hence `reusable: false`.

components.name: FlowEngine
components.description: 229 lines of an interpreter for flows defined in JSON: `agent-call`, `transform`, `conditional` and `validation` steps, with `skipTo` jumps out of conditional steps. Four flow definitions and four agent definitions sit as data, not code, but the constructor takes `WizardDbContext` and a concrete Azure OpenAI class directly, so the engine is nailed to one schema and one provider.

components.name: Prompt Wallet (rozszerzenie MV3)
components.description: 3,874 lines of JavaScript with no bundler, content scripts on eight AI chat hosts plus a separate one on github.com, with its own OAuth flow in `oauth-content.js`. `popup.js` alone is 2,863 lines and talks directly to the product's API.

components.name: AuthService
components.description: ASP.NET Identity with OpenIddict as the {{term:oidc}} server, Google and GitHub OAuth, organisations with invitations, quotas with a 429 response, PayPro billing as Merchant of Record, and GDPR data export and deletion. Identity here is glued to the billing of one pricing model.

components.name: AppHost (kompozycja Aspire)
components.description: A 474-line composition root that injects the JWT secret as an Aspire parameter and registers OAuth, Azure OpenAI, AI Foundry and SendGrid conditionally, only when they are configured. AgentTemplatesService is commented out here at line 200 and is nevertheless still built and tested in CI.

components.name: Web.Portal
components.description: The main Next.js 14 App Router application. The server-side API routes act as a proxy and keep the JWT in `HttpOnly` cookies (`app/api/auth/set-cookie/route.ts`). The Marketplace does the same — it has its own `set-cookie` and `/api/auth/session`, both called with `credentials: 'same-origin'`; in `localStorage` both applications keep nothing but `currentWorkspaceId`.

overlaps.reason: The whole E2E layer was deliberately moved out there. What is left here is a pointer in the documentation and a dead `playwright.config.ts` at the root as an artefact of the move.

The separate repo carries the same name as `AureliusPromptus.AuthService` and covers the same scope. That entry calls it a migration that never happened, and it is right: this is a copy, not a dependency.
`docs/test-automation-analysis.md` points there for the generalised acceptance-test rules produced by the audit here. The conclusions left, the debts stayed.
The architecture review names a twin document in that repository as a companion — the same self-assessment method applied to another system.
Web.OnePager serves exactly the same one-page-site function, only inside this monorepo.

product: The buyer is defined twice, and the second time more seriously. The first path is self-service SaaS with Free/Premium/Enterprise plans billed through PayPro as Merchant of Record; the code is there, the order models are there, the pricing page is there, and it is the variant with the lowest margin and the hardest acquisition. The second path is a private cloud licence for corporates: `docs/business/PRICING.md` quotes 29,900 PLN for Starter and 59,900 PLN for Professional plus deployments at 8,900–24,900 PLN, and `private-cloud-push.yml` is already a technically finished implementation of that model. It has to be noted, though, that the repository's own assessment of 17 August 2026 ends with the conclusion that none of the ten AI-infra niches examined is worth entering with this code, so the sales value lies in the platform layer and in the finished CRUD product, not in the AI layer.
highlights: `DatabaseProviderExtensions.cs` is 188 lines that switch between SQL Server, PostgreSQL and InMemory with a single switch, together with a retry policy and translation of the `.flycast` host to `.internal`. That is the concrete reason the migration from Azure to Fly.io did not require forking a single service.

24 Bicep modules give **every service its own managed identity and its own role assignments to SQL**, rather than one account shared by six services. It is a part that is rarely delivered, because it is dull and laborious.
`flyio.yml` is 86 KB: it detects changed services, deploys in an explicitly fixed dependency order and starts an ephemeral machine to provision agents as a versioned deployment artefact.
A Manifest V3 extension written by hand, with no bundler: 3,874 lines running on eight AI chat hosts plus github.com, with its own OAuth flow through a content script.

`docs/EMERGING_NICHES_EVALUATION.md` ends with the conclusion that **none of the ten niches examined is worth entering with this repository**, and itself points out a live tenant isolation bug with line numbers. I confirmed it independently in the code.
gaps: **The README is out of date to the point of being misleading.** It talks about .NET 8, although thirteen of the fourteen `.csproj` files are `net9.0`; it lists AgentInstancesService and `Web.NextJs`, which are not on disk; it describes Convex as the front end's backend. It does not mention Fly.io, the Marketplace, the OnePager, the AdminDashboard or the browser extension.

No LICENSE file at the root, and the licence section in the README is literally `[Add your license information here]`. The only {{term:mit}} file sits in a front-end subdirectory and can be read as covering the whole thing.

The E2E tests are not wired into any workflow in either of the two repositories, and the author's own audit estimates that around 45% of them never reach a real assertion. A green run would mean nothing, and `playwright.config.ts` at the root points at a directory that does not exist.

No address has been confirmed as answering. There are ten `fly.toml` files, a parallel Azure Container Apps path and a private cloud variant, but the application names diverge between the toml files (`aureliuspromptus-*`) and the destroying workflow (`aurelius-*`), so `destroy` may not hit what exists.

Dead code kept alive in CI: AgentTemplatesService commented out in `AppHost.cs:200` but still built and tested, and 37 KB of a per-PR environments workflow with a commented-out trigger. Separately there is `AureliusPromptus.ApiService/` — a project with no entry in `AureliusPromptus.sln`, no registration in `AppHost.cs` and no `fly.toml`; it appears only as a path filter in `pr-validation.yml`, so nothing builds or deploys it. At 74 documents and one author the {{term:drift}} is already visible — two documents mark themselves as superseded.
next: Add `AuthorizationOptions.FallbackPolicy` with `RequireAuthenticatedUser` in PromptTemplatesService, AgentTemplatesService and MarketplaceService, and reconcile the `org_id` claim name looked up in `ApiControllerBase` with the `organization` actually emitted. That is one sitting and it closes the most serious item on this list.
Write the README from scratch against the actual tree. The current one does more harm than no README at all, because it is the first thing a private cloud client will see.
Add a LICENSE at the root, or state outright that the repository is proprietary. When you are selling licences at 29,900–59,900 PLN a year that is not an editorial detail.
Delete the dead `playwright.config.ts` and the `test:e2e` scripts that lead nowhere, or rewrite them against real directories.
Cut ServiceDefaults out into a separate, versioned package without `KonradPromptSeeds.cs`. It is the only asset in this repository that makes sense outside this product.
risks: **Confirmed missing authorisation.** `PromptTemplatesController` has no `[Authorize]` on the class or on `GetAll`/`GetPaged`, and a grep for `FallbackPolicy` returns nothing across the whole solution. `GetAll` takes `workspaceId` straight from the query string, so template content is readable across the workspace boundary without authentication. The {{term:blast|blast radius}} covers every tenant at once.

**This entry was repeating an out-of-date line of documentation.** `docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md` item 1.1 (status OPEN, priority CRITICAL) still claims that the Marketplace keeps the access and refresh token in `localStorage`. The code does not do that: `AureliusPromptus.Web.Marketplace/contexts/auth-context.tsx` keeps the tokens in memory and in `HttpOnly` cookies set by `/api/auth/set-cookie` (`httpOnly: true` in three places in the route), says so in its own comment, and on start-up migrates older copies out of `localStorage` into cookies and removes them. The only `localStorage.setItem` in this application is `currentWorkspaceId`, the cookie banner and the contact form's rate-limit key. The real risk is documentation diverging from the code: item 1.1 lands on the deployment blocker list and directs attention at a problem that has been fixed.

Email confirmation is switched off at registration (`EmailConfirmed = true` hard-coded, `RequireConfirmedEmail = false`). On a paid product that is a straight route to free-account abuse and to GDPR problems.

No licence at the root while private cloud licences are being sold is a real legal hole. On top of that a name collision: the separate `authservice` repo is named the same as the service inside this monorepo, which confuses the portfolio map.
headline: The deployment is the best part, not the AI — `PromptTemplatesController` has no `[Authorize]`
